slug: 2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps

facts.fact: ANATS's coordinator of cooperation and civil registration told the ID4Africa 2025 meeting that more than 120,000 children have been registered through hospital-based registry offices since the civil registration system was integrated with health facilities in 2023; no date is given for the count, so the document's publication date is used.

The account gives 97 digitised hospital-based civil registration points at present, which the government plans to raise to 600 in the next few years; no total of local offices is given and no date for the count, so the document's publication date is used.

ANATS's coordinator says the system connects civil registry offices, hospitals, vaccination centres, municipalities, mobile units, refugee camps and schools, with all data sent by SMS to the national agency, which validates it and sends it back for issuance; undated, so the document's publication date is used.

The system is described as ANATS's own by the agency's coordinator of cooperation and civil registration, with data validated at the national agency; undated, so the document's publication date is used.

systems.platform: data transfer by SMS to the national agency; mobile phones with an ANATS application
systems.tiers: civil registry offices, hospitals, vaccination centres, municipalities, mobile units, refugee camps and schools; 97 digitised hospital-based registration points, planned to reach 600

systems.system: Community health workers recording births in rural areas
systems.tiers: rural areas, as intermediaries to the hospital-based registry offices; said to ensure coverage of about 70 per cent of the rural population
primary and secondary schools; more than 180,000 pupils registered since 2023
nomadic populations; with biometric registration missions for older people; the document does not say the mobile teams are permanent

note: The 'made' value rests on the speaker's description of SMS transfer to the national agency at registration; the document does not say whether the hospital points keep a paper register alongside. The 97 points are hospital-based, not commune offices.
